articles.title: Garment workers in Bangladesh take their struggle for decent wages to the streets
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content_excerpt: For multiple days, thousands of workers in Bangladesh, mostly from garment factories, protested for a raise in their minimum monthly wages and against the rising prices of essential commodities, defying the state’s oppressive measures. On Tuesday, November 3, news reports indicated fresh clashes between workers and security forces at various places in the capital, Dhaka, with the agitating workers trying to block highways and other roads. The protests broke out despite the Home Minister of the country Salahuddin Ahmed warning the workers to return to work on Monday after claiming their demands had been addressed by the government through the formation of a “wage board.” Meanwhile, the authorities unleashed violence and repression on workers with police resorting to baton charges and firing

articles.title: India in the Mediterranean
articles.author: Zoe.
articles.content_excerpt: On October 26, 2026, Greece’s Foreign Minister George Gerapetritis stood at the United Nations headquarters and rejected the maritime agreement between Turkey and Libya. Gerapetritis spoke on behalf of Greece of course, but also Bahrain, Cyprus, Egypt, the European Union, and the United Arab Emirates. Five days later, the Indian frigate INS Trishul entered Souda Bay in Crete as part of activities with the US Navy installation (Naval Support Activity) and with the NATO Maritime Interdiction Operational Training Center. The sequence illuminates a developing strategic geography: India’s naval reach, its confrontation with Pakistan’s new Turkish partner, and its ambition to connect Indian capital to European markets increasingly converge in the eastern Mediterranean. articles.title: “Hatemonger” as Chief of Staff: Trump Taps Stephen Miller to Top Role After Massive Election Defeat
articles.content_excerpt: Stephen Miller, the architect of the Trump administration’s mass deportation policies, has replaced Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff. In a recent 60 Minutes interview, President Donald Trump acknowledged that his immigration policies may be “too tough” and contributed to his party’s steep losses in the midterm elections, but in elevating Miller, he is “choosing to double down,” says journalist Jean Guerrero. “Stephen Miller enables [Trump] in this instinct to choose cruelty over everything else,” she says. Guerrero is a New York Times contributing opinion writer, USC journalism professor and author of Hatemonger: Stephen Miller, Donald Trump, and the White Nationalist Agenda .

articles.title: “A Crackdown on All Independent Voices”: Egypt Shutters News Outlets, Prosecutes Editor Lina Attalah
articles.content_excerpt: Lina Attalah, editor-in-chief of Egypt’s leading independent news outlet Mada Masr , faces a criminal trial this week on charges of “spreading false information,” just two weeks after being convicted of operating an unlicensed website and fined more than $50,000. A judge also ordered the publication to be shut down. The cases are part of a broader crackdown on independent Egyptian media under the government of President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, including the arrest of the entire newsroom of another outlet, _ Matsadaash_. articles.title: Gaza faces an uncertain future a year into the ‘ceasefire’
articles.author: Ruwaida Amer
articles.content_excerpt: Two million people in the Gaza Strip have been forced by the Israeli military into an area covering approximately 30% of the territory. Now, with the onset of winter, Gazan families are not only facing constant displacement, but are facing flooding in their tents. The “yellow zone” began to emerge gradually alongside the presence of the Israeli military. It encompasses areas near the Gaza-Israel border, stretching along the entire frontier from the north of the Gaza Strip to the south. As the war continued persisting into October 2025 this zone expanded significantly.
